cast.name: Lord Ashcombe
cast.bio: Peer of the realm, Suite Imperiale. Collects clocks and grievances.

cast.name: Paul Sernine
cast.bio: Rentier. Nobody has ever seen him pay for anything.

cast.name: Horace Velmont
cast.bio: Painter of society portraits. Paints mostly at night.

cast.name: Raul Ortega
cast.bio: Cattle baron. Signs everything with a flourish and an R.

cast.name: Ines de Almagro
cast.bio: Widow. Travels with eleven trunks and one maid.

cast.name: Rupert Blakeney
cast.bio: Gentleman of leisure from Bath. Excellent coat.

wrong_suspects.paul sernine: An anagram, Ganimard? Lupin is vain, not stupid. Sernine is released with apologies.
wrong_suspects.horace velmont: Velmont was painting the Prefect's wife at the hour of the theft. The Prefect confirms it, twice.
wrong_suspects.raul ortega: Senor Ortega produces a receipt for the champagne and a lawyer for everything else.
wrong_suspects.ines almagro: The Senora faints. The maid does not. Neither is Lupin.
wrong_suspects.ashcombe: You arrest the peer in the neighbouring suite. He is the Prefect's cousin. Awkward.
wrong_suspects.arsene lupin: Yes. Under which name? That is rather the question.
wrong_suspects.grey: Mr. Grey checked out this morning. The concierge is certain, because Mr. Grey tipped him.
wrong_suspects.ganimard: The inspector reads your note, takes off his hat, and puts it back on. 'Out.'

wrong_default: Ganimard reads your note twice and lights his pipe. 'No.'
The clerk before you was dismissed for less. Try again.
Not that, mon petit. Look at the data again.

chapters.title: The Night of the 17th
chapters.story: Paris, May 1912. The Comtesse de Cagliostro wakes at the Ritz to find her sapphire, the Blue Star, gone and a calling card on the pillow: A. L. Inspector Ganimard has been called at three in the morning and is in no mood. You are his clerk. He drops a stack of police reports on your desk. 'Find ours.'
chapters.objective: Find the police report for the theft at the Hotel Ritz on 18 May 1912 (dates are written 19120518).
chapters.telegram: MY DEAR GANIMARD STOP YOU FOUND THE REPORT STOP THE BALCONY WAS DELIGHTFUL STOP ASK WHO PAYS THE MOST STOP A L
hints: The concierge, without looking up: 'Reports? The Prefecture keeps them all in one ledger, monsieur. police_report, they call it.'
The chambermaid: 'Three thousand reports, and you read them all? Ask only for the Ritz, only that date, only a theft. WHERE, monsieur, as they say.'
Ganimard's notebook: SELECT id FROM police_report WHERE place = '____' AND date = ____ AND type = 'theft'

chapters.title: The Neighbouring Suite
chapters.story: 'The thief came over the balcony of the neighbouring suite, the most expensive one on the floor,' Ganimard reads aloud, as if the report had insulted him. The Ritz keeps a register: every guest, every suite, every price, since January. Six months of it, and the prices on the second floor are all within a few francs of each other. 'The name of whoever slept in the priciest suite on the second floor on the night of the 17th. Not the second priciest. The priciest.'
chapters.objective: In hotel_register, find the guest on floor 2 whose stay covers the night of 17 May 1912 (checkin <= 19120517 and checkout > 19120517) and who pays the highest price.
chapters.telegram: MY DEAR GANIMARD STOP HIS LORDSHIP SNORES STOP I CROSSED HIS BALCONY TWICE AND HE NEVER STIRRED STOP HIS VALET SLEEPS LESS STOP ASK HIM ABOUT MY COAT STOP A L
hints: The concierge: 'The register, monsieur? hotel_register. Guest, suite, floor, price, checkin, checkout. We write the guest's name in full, as one does.'

The chambermaid: 'Ten thousand lines and you want one? Keep the second floor and that night, then sort by price, the dearest first: ORDER BY price DESC. Then LIMIT 1, monsieur, as the head waiter says when the Baron asks for more.'
Ganimard's notebook: SELECT guest_name FROM hotel_register WHERE floor = ____ AND checkin <= 19120517 AND checkout > 19120517 ORDER BY ____ DESC LIMIT ____

chapters.title: A Plate Beginning With 75-2
chapters.story: His Lordship, when woken, is displeased but useful. His valet saw a man in an English coat leave by the service door and take a motor-cab on the Place Vendome. The plate began with 75-2; the rest, he says, was in the dark, and the fellow tipped in English coins. 'Forty cabs in Paris begin with 75-2,' says Ganimard. 'The company keeps a book. Find me the one that left the Place Vendome after two in the morning.'
chapters.objective: Read the neighbour's statement in interview, then find in cab_ride the ride picked up at Place Vendome on 19120518 after 02:00 (time >= 200) whose plate begins with 75-2.
chapters.telegram: MY DEAR GANIMARD STOP THE CAB SMELLED OF CIGARS STOP THE DRIVER KNOWS THE WAY STOP HE HAS TAKEN ME THERE BEFORE STOP READ HIS WEEK STOP A L
hints: The concierge: 'Statements go in interview, monsieur, and cabs in cab_ride: plate, date, time, pickup, dropoff. The company is very proud of its book.'

The chambermaid: 'You do not know the whole plate? Then do not ask for the whole plate. LIKE, monsieur, with the percent sign for the part you do not know: plate LIKE '75-2%'. And say where and when, or you will get forty.'
Ganimard's notebook: SELECT plate FROM cab_ride WHERE plate LIKE '____%' AND pickup = '____' AND date = 19120518 AND time >= ____

chapters.title: The Cab's Week
chapters.story: The driver of the cab has a bad memory and a good book. Ganimard reads the week before the theft: sixty fares, the 13th to the 19th. 'A thief with a plan visits his fence before the job. Twice. Three times. Find me the address this cab dropped at three times or more that week. I do not want the list. I want the address.'
chapters.objective: In cab_ride, for the plate you found in chapter 3, between 19120513 and 19120519, find the dropoff address visited at least three times.
chapters.telegram: MY DEAR GANIMARD STOP THREE TIMES TO THE SAME DOOR STOP HABIT IS THE ENEMY OF ART STOP THE HOUSE HAS FIVE TENANTS AND ONE OF THEM OWNS A LOUPE STOP A L
hints: The concierge: 'Same book, monsieur. cab_ride. Sixty lines for that plate that week. The dropoff column is the one to count.'

The chambermaid: 'Counting by hand is for constables. GROUP BY dropoff, and COUNT(*). Then keep only the groups with three or more: HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3. WHERE cannot do it, monsieur, WHERE does not know how to count.'
Ganimard's notebook: SELECT dropoff FROM cab_ride WHERE plate = '____' AND date BETWEEN 19120513 AND 19120519 GROUP BY ____ HAVING COUNT(*) >= ____

chapters.title: The Boarding House
chapters.story: The address is a boarding house: five tenants and a landlady who has seen nothing since 1889. Ganimard wants the tenant whose trade is jeweller; every fence in Paris calls himself a jeweller. 'Persons are in one ledger, addresses in another. The Prefecture has never put the two together. You will.'
chapters.objective: Join person to address (person.address_id = address.id). Find the tenant at the address of chapter 4 (number and street are two columns of address) whose occupation is jeweller.
chapters.telegram: MY DEAR GANIMARD STOP GRIMAUD PAID ME WELL AND PROMPTLY STOP HE BANKS AT THE CREDIT LYONNAIS STOP HE PAYS A GREAT MANY PEOPLE STOP ADD IT UP STOP A L
hints: The concierge: 'The Prefecture keeps person, with the occupation, and address, with the number and the street. Each person carries an address_id. That is the thread, monsieur.'

The chambermaid: 'Two ledgers, one question: JOIN address AS a ON p.address_id = a.id. Then WHERE the number, the street and the occupation. Without the occupation you arrest five people, and one of them is a seamstress.'
Ganimard's notebook: SELECT p.name FROM person AS p JOIN address AS a ON p.address_id = a.id WHERE a.number = ____ AND a.street = '____' AND p.occupation = '____'

chapters.title: Follow the Francs
chapters.story: The jeweller keeps an account at the Credit Lyonnais and, since Ganimard has a warrant, the bank keeps nothing from him. Twenty-four payments in May, to a dozen people. 'A fence pays a thief in pieces, so the bank does not blink. Do not show me the biggest cheque, that is what he wants you to see. Show me the account that received the most from him in total this month.'
chapters.objective: Join person, bank_account (bank_account.person_id = person.id) and bank_transaction (bank_transaction.account_id = bank_account.id). For the jeweller of chapter 5, in May 1912 (date between 19120501 and 19120531), find the counterparty_id that received the largest total amount.
chapters.telegram: MY DEAR GANIMARD STOP THE SUM NOT THE LARGEST STOP YOU ARE LEARNING STOP I CONFIRMED RECEIPT BY WIRE FROM THE RITZ DESK BEFORE DAWN STOP THE CLERK THERE READS NOTHING STOP A L
hints: The concierge: 'Three ledgers this time, monsieur: person, then bank_account, then bank_transaction. counterparty_id is who received the money. The bank is very proud of its columns.'

The chambermaid: 'Two JOINs in a row, one ON each. Then GROUP BY counterparty_id, SUM(amount), and ORDER BY that sum, DESC. The largest single payment is a decoy, monsieur. Fences are not stupid, only greedy.'

Ganimard's notebook: SELECT t.counterparty_id FROM person AS p JOIN bank_account AS b ON b.person_id = p.id JOIN bank_transaction AS t ON t.account_id = b.id WHERE p.name = '____' AND t.date BETWEEN 19120501 AND 19120531 GROUP BY t.counterparty_id ORDER BY ____(t.amount) DESC LIMIT ____

chapters.title: A Wire Before Dawn
chapters.story: The Ritz telegraph desk sent eighty wires on the 18th and its clerk is too proud to have read any of them. Ganimard has his own idea of a day: night before six, morning before noon, afternoon before six, evening after that. 'Sort them into my four boxes and bring me the one sent at night. The sender confirms a payment to the account you found in chapter 6. He signs with one letter, which is one more than he needs.'
chapters.objective: In telegram, for office Ritz on 19120518, classify each wire by time as night (before 0600), morning (before 1200), afternoon (before 1800) or evening, and find the single one sent at night.
chapters.telegram: MY DEAR GANIMARD STOP YOU READ MY WIRE STOP AS ALWAYS MY FIRST ORDER BEFORE DAWN STOP A MAN OF HABIT IS A MAN WITH A ROOM NUMBER STOP A L
hints: The concierge: 'The desk keeps telegram: office, date, time, sender, recipient, text. Times are four digits stored as a number, monsieur: 245 is a quarter to three in the morning.'

The chambermaid: 'Four boxes from one number? CASE WHEN time < 600 THEN 'night' WHEN time < 1200 THEN 'morning' and so on, END AS period. Put it in a subquery, monsieur, then WHERE period = 'night'. The inspector likes his boxes.'

Ganimard's notebook: SELECT id FROM (SELECT id, CASE WHEN time < ____ THEN 'night' WHEN time < 1200 THEN 'morning' WHEN time < 1800 THEN 'afternoon' ELSE 'evening' END AS period FROM telegram WHERE office = '____' AND date = 19120518) AS t WHERE period = '____'

chapters.title: The First Order Before Dawn
chapters.story: 'As always my first order before dawn.' Ganimard underlines it. 'A man of habit. The Ritz keeps a room-service ledger. Find me the suite whose FIRST order of the 18th was Clicquot 1904, before six. Not any order. The first.' Senor Ortega, you recall, also likes champagne.
chapters.objective: Using room_service for 19120518, rank each suite's orders by time. Find the suite whose rank-1 order is Clicquot 1904 before 06:00, then the guest registered in that suite on floor 2 that night.
chapters.telegram: MY DEAR GANIMARD STOP GARE DU NORD NINE FIFTEEN STOP DO NOT BE LATE STOP THE BLUE STAR SENDS REGARDS FROM LONDON STOP CHAPTER IX IF YOU DARE STOP A L
hints: The concierge: 'Room service writes everything in room_service: suite, time, item. The register tells you who sleeps where.'
The chambermaid: 'First order per suite, monsieur? That is a RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY suite ORDER BY time). Then keep rank 1. Then the register.'

Ganimard's notebook: SELECT guest_name FROM hotel_register WHERE floor = 2 AND checkin <= 19120518 AND checkout > 19120518 AND suite = (SELECT suite FROM (SELECT suite, item, time, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY ____ ORDER BY ____) AS rk FROM room_service WHERE date = 19120518) AS ranked WHERE rk = 1 AND item = '____' AND time < 600)

chapters.title: The Trunk
chapters.story: Ganimard has gone home to his cat. You have not. The Blue Star 'sends regards from London': the boat train left the Gare du Nord on the 19th and Lord Ashcombe was on it, with his trunks. So was somebody else's ticket. Every trunk in the baggage car is entered under an owner's name and a ticket number, and nobody at the Compagnie du Nord checks that the two agree. Find the trunk that says Ashcombe on the label but travelled on a ticket bought by a man who is not Ashcombe.
chapters.objective: Using a CTE, list the trunks in luggage whose owner_name is Lord Ashcombe together with the person_id of their train_ticket, then keep the one whose ticket holder (in person) is not Lord Ashcombe.
chapters.answer_form: the trunk number (a letter, a dash, a digit)
chapters.telegram: MY DEAR CLERK STOP HIS LORDSHIP CARRIED THE STONE THROUGH CUSTOMS WITH A CLEAR CONSCIENCE STOP THE TICKET WAS BOUGHT BY A REGULAR STOP YOU HAVE NEVER SEEN US TOGETHER STOP A L
hints: The night porter, who has replaced the concierge: 'Baggage is luggage, monsieur: trunk_no, owner_name, ticket_id. The ticket is train_ticket, and it carries a person_id.'

The chambermaid: 'Name your first step: WITH ashcombe_trunks AS (luggage JOIN train_ticket ON the ticket_id, WHERE the owner is his Lordship). Then JOIN that to person and keep WHERE p.name is NOT his Lordship. A CTE is a drawer, monsieur. You fill it, then you open it.'

Ganimard's notebook: WITH ashcombe_trunks AS (SELECT l.trunk_no, t.person_id FROM luggage AS l JOIN train_ticket AS t ON l.ticket_id = t.id WHERE l.owner_name = '____') SELECT trunk_no FROM ashcombe_trunks AS a JOIN person AS p ON a.person_id = p.id WHERE p.name <> '____'

chapters.title: Never Seen Together
chapters.story: The ticket was bought for cash. The clerk remembers only 'a regular, monsieur, English, excellent coat', which describes half the second floor. The Ritz has a handful of regulars who have stayed often since January. So has Mr. Blakeney. You have a suspicion of the theatrical kind: two names, one man, and a man cannot sleep in two suites on the same night. Among the regular guests, six stays or more, find the one who has never once been in the hotel on the same night as Blakeney. Beware: the Baron and Mr. Bell each crossed him for exactly one night, and one night is enough to be two people.
chapters.objective: In hotel_register, among guests with at least 6 stays, find the one (other than Rupert Blakeney) whose stays never overlap a stay of Rupert Blakeney. Two stays overlap when x.checkin < y.checkout AND y.checkin < x.checkout.
chapters.telegram: MY DEAR CLERK STOP GREY IN THE ODD WEEKS BLAKENEY IN THE EVEN STOP THE CONCIERGE NEVER NOTICED STOP ON THE NIGHT OF THE 17TH MY SUITE WAS VERY QUIET FOR ONE HOUR STOP A L
hints: The night porter: 'Only hotel_register, monsieur. Six months of it. A regular is a name that comes back six times. We do not ask why.'

The chambermaid: 'First the regulars: GROUP BY guest_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 6, in a subquery. Then for each, NOT EXISTS a pair of stays, his and Blakeney's, that overlap: x.checkin < y.checkout AND y.checkin < x.checkout. Not one night, monsieur.'

Ganimard's notebook: SELECT g.guest_name FROM (SELECT guest_name FROM hotel_register GROUP BY guest_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= ____) AS g WHERE g.guest_name <> '____' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hotel_register AS x JOIN hotel_register AS y ON x.guest_name = '____' AND y.guest_name = g.guest_name WHERE x.checkin < y.checkout AND y.checkin < x.checkout)

chapters.title: The Silence
chapters.story: Every suite makes noise at night: the lift boy writes down who rings, room service writes down who is thirsty, the telegraph desk writes down who wires, and charges it to the suite. Put the three ledgers together for the night of the 18th, suite by suite, in order of time. Somewhere on the second floor a suite fell silent at 02:05, when the lift went down, and woke at 03:10, when it came back up; the porter heard it at 02:10. Suite 407 slept longer, but later. That is not your suite.
chapters.objective: Combine lift_log, room_service and telegram (rows with a suite) for 19120518 before 06:00 into one list of (suite, time). With LAG(time) OVER (PARTITION BY suite ORDER BY time), find the suite that has an event at or before 02:05 (205) and its next event at or after 03:10 (310).
chapters.telegram: MY DEAR CLERK STOP ONE HOUR AND FIVE MINUTES STOP THE BALCONY THE STONE THE CAB THE JEWELLER AND BACK FOR CHAMPAGNE STOP AND THE FORTY THOUSAND FRANCS STOP WHERE DO YOU THINK THEY WENT STOP A L
hints: The night porter: 'The lift boy keeps lift_log: date, time, floor, suite. Room service you know. Telegrams charged to a suite carry the suite number, monsieur; the others carry nothing.'

The chambermaid: 'UNION ALL the three into one CTE of suite and time. Then LAG(time) OVER (PARTITION BY suite ORDER BY time) gives each event its previous one. A silence is a row whose prev is at or before 205 and whose time is at or after 310. Do not look for the longest silence, monsieur. Look for the right one.'

Ganimard's notebook: WITH ev AS (SELECT suite, time FROM lift_log WHERE date = 19120518 AND time < 600 UNION ALL SELECT suite, time FROM room_service WHERE date = 19120518 AND time < 600 UNION ALL SELECT suite, time FROM telegram WHERE date = 19120518 AND time < 600 AND suite IS NOT NULL), gaps AS (SELECT suite, time, ____(time) OVER (PARTITION BY ____ ORDER BY time) AS prev FROM ev) SELECT suite FROM gaps WHERE prev <= ____ AND time >= 310

chapters.title: Follow the Money
chapters.story: The last of the forty thousand francs reached the shell account of chapter 6 on the 21st; the first of it had already left on the 20th. From there the money moves every three days, less two percent at every door, through shell accounts at four banks, into June. One hop was paid in two halves. One shell account did other business the same day. Follow the ninety-eight percent, and only the ninety-eight percent, seven doors down, and read the name on the last account. Ganimard will not like it.
chapters.objective: With a recursive CTE, start from the account of chapter 6 with 40000 F at hop 0 and follow, hop by hop, the transfer (or the sum of the transfers between the same two accounts) whose amount is within 1 F of 98% of the previous hop, using bank_transaction from 19120518 on. Find the person who owns the account at hop 7.
chapters.telegram: MY DEAR GANIMARD STOP INSURANCE PAYS THREE HUNDRED THOUSAND FOR A STONE WORTH FORTY THOUSAND STOP ARITHMETIC IS THE GREATEST OF CRIMES STOP A L
hints: The night porter: 'The money is in bank_transaction, monsieur: account_id pays counterparty_id. bank_account tells you whose account it is, when it is anybody's. Most of them are nobody's.'

The chambermaid: 'First a CTE that SUMs the transfers per account_id and counterparty_id, because one hop was split. Then WITH RECURSIVE chain(account_id, amount, hop): the anchor is the shell account and its forty thousand at hop 0; each step joins the sums and keeps ABS(amount - previous * 0.98) <= 1. Hop 7, then bank_account, then person.'

Ganimard's notebook: WITH RECURSIVE flows AS (SELECT account_id, counterparty_id, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM bank_transaction WHERE date >= 19120518 AND type = 'transfer' GROUP BY account_id, counterparty_id), chain(account_id, amount, hop) AS (SELECT ____, 40000, 0 UNION ALL SELECT f.counterparty_id, f.amount, c.hop + 1 FROM chain AS c JOIN flows AS f ON f.account_id = c.account_id WHERE ABS(f.amount - c.amount * ____) <= 1) SELECT p.name FROM chain AS c JOIN bank_account AS b ON b.id = c.account_id JOIN person AS p ON p.id = b.person_id WHERE c.hop = ____

endings.part1: Gare du Nord, 20 May, 09:10. Ganimard's hand falls on the shoulder of Rupert Blakeney, Esq. The gentleman turns, smiles, and hands the inspector a small velvet case. It is empty. 'You have my name, Inspector. The Blue Star has a train to catch.' Behind him, the boat train pulls out.
endings.part2: The Comtesse receives Ganimard in her suite, now insured for three hundred thousand francs. She offers tea. Ganimard declines, which is a first. You are promoted to a desk with a window. Lupin, in London, sends a telegram.
